transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hi Mr. Park, it is good to see you again. Please, have a seat.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thanks.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Before we go over your recovery and the next steps, there is something I need to discuss with you regarding the contrast dye we used during your scan last week.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh, okay. Was there something wrong with the scan?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The scan itself was fine, but there was a mistake in how we handled your care. We gave you the contrast agent when we should not have. I am very sorry for this. I take full responsibility for this error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait, what do you mean? Like, it was the wrong medicine?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, it was the right dye for the test, but based on your blood work, your kidneys were already under a lot of stress. We should have followed a specific safety protocol to protect your kidneys before giving you that dye, and we failed to do that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't really know what that means. What happens now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is a lot to take in. Basically, because we didn't do the pre-treatment, there is a risk that the dye could have caused further damage to your kidney function.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I... I didn't even know my kidneys were stressed. Is that why I felt so tired?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It could be a contributing factor. I can see that you look really overwhelmed right now, and it makes total sense that you'd feel that way, especially since you're managing all of this on your own for the first time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yeah. I just... I didn't want to call my parents because I wanted to show them I could do this. Now I don't even know if I'm okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It sounds like you've been trying really hard to be independent and take this on yourself, and now you're feeling like that's being threatened by something that wasn't your fault.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I guess. Are my kidneys going to fail?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can't give you a definitive answer right this second, but we are monitoring you very closely to make sure we catch any changes immediately.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So, what did you actually do wrong? Like, did the machine mess up?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, the machine was fine. The information was right there in your chart, but the team and I missed it. We didn't check the creatinine levels against the protocol. That was our mistake.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't even know if I should be mad. I just... I trust you guys.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That trust is exactly why I feel so terrible about this. You trusted us with your health, and we let you down. I am truly sorry.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is there a way to fix it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right now, we need to manage it. I want to get you back for another blood draw this Friday to check those levels again.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Friday. Okay. What else?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm going to check your chart again to see if we need to adjust your fluids. I'll probably have you drink more water than usual for the next few days.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Like, how much?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll have the nurse give you a specific amount of liters per day to hit.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Do I need to do anything else?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just keep track of how much you're urinating and let me know if you see any blood or if the color changes.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay. I can do that.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll have my coordinator call you tomorrow just to check in and make sure you have the appointment time for Friday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay. Thank you.

H.justification: Resident allows patient to finish all turns, maintains a steady pace during emotional distress, and uses no rushing language.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly and lay language was used, but there were no comprehension checks (e.g., 'Does that make sense?') throughout the transcript.

A.justification: Resident uses direct apology language ('I am very sorry'), takes full responsibility ('I take full responsibility'), and maintains this without deflection.

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions ('overwhelmed', 'feeling like that's being threatened') and references the patient's specific struggle with independence.

T.justification: Resident provides specific next steps with timelines (blood draw Friday, coordinator call tomorrow) and patient roles (drink water, track urination), but does not address how to prevent the error in the future.
